The largest desert in the world is **Antarctica**, covering about 14.2 million square kilometers (5.5 million square miles). A desert is defined by low precipitation rather than heat, and Antarctica receives very little, averaging roughly 200 mm (8 inches) annually along the coast and far less inland.

The largest *hot* desert is the **Sahara** in northern Africa, spanning about 9.2 million square kilometers (3.6 million square miles). The Arctic is the second-largest cold desert, at around 13.9 million square kilometers.

So the answer depends on whether you're counting all deserts or just hot ones.
